extracted.intended_audience: readers/buyers of books; artists, designers, and researchers seeking illustrated reference works
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher's catalogue / book-advertisement pages describing newly issued and forthcoming illustrated reference and literary works, with notes on scope, format, and intended use (Victorian-era listings).

rubrics_metrics.name: History of Costume — glossarial form and artist focus
rubrics_metrics.description: That this work appears in a glossarial form arises from the desire of many artists who have expressed to me the difficulty they constantly meet with in their endeavours to ascertain the complete form of a garment, or the exact mode of fastening a piece of armour, or buckling of a belt, from their study of a sepulchral effigy or a figure in an illumination; the attitude of the personages represented, or the disposition of other portions of their attire, effectually preventing the requisite examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should gather all that is known or suggested by competent writers; present material in a glossarial (dictionary) form for ease of lookup by artists; re-examine authorities where contradictory; avoid misleading the reader; consolidate pith of many foreign publications; supply illustrations and practical descriptions that help artists determine garment forms and fastenings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclopaedia of Costume — publication and illustration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: This work will be published in Twenty-four Monthly Parts, quarto, at Five Shillings, profusely illustrated by Plates and Wood Engravings; with each Part will also be issued a splendid Coloured Plate, from an original Painting or Miniature, of Royal and Noble Personages, and National Costume, both original and domestic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comprehensive costume cyclopaedia for artists and scholars should be issued in parts, be profusely illustrated (including splendid coloured plates from originals), and cover national and domestic costume; format and regular issued parts are emphasized (monthly quarto parts at a stated price).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handbook of Heraldry — essential contents and features
rubrics_metrics.description: Directions for Tracing Pedigrees. 2. Deciphering Ancient mss., illustrated by alphabets and facsimiles. 3. The Appointment of Liveries. 4. Continental and American Heraldry, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A best-practice heraldry handbook should include practical instructions for pedigree tracing, tools for deciphering ancient manuscripts (alphabets, facsimiles), rules for appointment of liveries, and coverage of continental and American heraldry; richly illustrated (360 plates and woodcuts in the advertised edition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Englishman's House — practical guide features
rubrics_metrics.description: It gives every variety of houses, from a workman's cottage to a nobleman's palace. The book is intended to supply a plain, non-technical account of every style of house, with the cost and manner of building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical guide to selecting or building a house should be non-technical, cover the full variety of house types, include costs and methods of building, and be heavily illustrated (nearly 600 illustrations called out for this edition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Book of Hall-Marks — practical testing methods
rubrics_metrics.description: This work gives practical methods for testing the quality of gold and silver. It was compiled by the author for his own use, and as a Supplement to 'Chaffers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A manual for goldsmiths/silversmiths should include practical, usable tests for assessing metal quality and clear plates of hall-marks (46 plates in this edition) to support identification and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising, A History of — desirable contents for an advertising history
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrated by Anecdotes, Curious Specimens, Biographical Notes, and Examples of Successful Advertisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A history of advertising intended as a companion to signboard histories should include entertaining and informative elements: anecdotes, curious advertising specimens, biographical notes on advertisers, and concrete examples of successful advertising practices; should be illustrated (coloured frontispiece and numerous illustrations) and accessible in crown 8vo format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heraldic/Costume reference — use of facsimiles and alphabets
rubrics_metrics.description: The books supplying any such information [on costume or heraldry] are very few, and the best confined to armour or ecclesiastical costume. The only English publication of the kind ... contains a glossary, the most valuable portion whereof are the quotations from old plays, mediaeval romances, and satirical ballads, containing allusions to various articles of attire in fashion at the time of their composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference works in these domains should include primary-source quotations, facsimiles, alphabets, and glossary entries to make obscure historical terminology and forms intelligible and usable to artists, historians, and students.

rubrics_metrics.name: County History — attention to family history
rubrics_metrics.description: An entirely new History of this important County, great attention being given to all matters pertaining to Family History.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A county history intended for serious use should devote substantial attention to family history and genealogical matters, be produced with high-quality plates (copper and stone) and abundant illustrations, and be issued in parts for collectors/researchers.
